features: THE THOUSANDTH NOBODY HAD FILLED IN — No migration: the database is not touched. A millesimal table in which a unit is linked but its value is still empty produced an instalment plan that did not contain that unit at all: not a € 0.00 row to explain, nothing whatsoever. And since the engine always allocates 100% of the expense, dividing it by the table's actual sum — not by 1000 — its share was paid by the others. Measured: ten units, nine filled in and one forgotten, each of the nine pays € 1,111.11 instead of € 1,000.00, with the leftover cent falling on one of them, and the plan's total stays identical to the budget, so no accounting check had anything to report.

THE GENERATION NOW STOPS, says which unit and in which table, and takes you to the thousandths page. You can go ahead all the same — the decision stays the administrator's — but by writing down why, which stays on the plan's record and opens an Inbox reminder. The warning does not correct, it warns: whoever goes ahead takes on the allocation as it was, and the remedy is to fill the thousandth in.

WHY IT COULD NOT BE SEEN BEFORE. The thousandths field was mandatory, so an empty box could not be saved: it looked like a defence and it was not. Whoever ticked «Link all properties» while creating a table found every row empty and a page that could no longer be saved until every box had been filled in — and the quickest way out was to write 0 where the value was not known yet. But 0, to the program, means «this unit does not take part», which is how genuine partial tables work: the lift without the ground floors, the stairs without the shops that open onto the street. The requirement did not prevent the mistake, it funnelled it into a shape indistinguishable from a deliberate choice.

FROM THIS VERSION THE THOUSANDTH CAN BE LEFT EMPTY: you link the units today and fill the values in when they arrive from the surveyor, over several sittings if need be. And empty means empty, not zero. Row absent: the unit does not take part. Value zero: the unit does not take part, said explicitly — legitimate, and no warning. Value empty: not filled in yet, and it is the only case that warns.

THE PAGE NO LONGER DECLARES ITSELF FINISHED WHEN IT IS NOT. With every unit linked and no thousandth written, the header said «All linked» and the total said 0.00 without commenting on it. Now, when there is nothing left to link but values are missing, the counter says how many rows are still to be filled in. And the footer counts units, not rows: before, an empty row figured among the «linked units».

LINKING SEVERAL UNITS AT ONCE, from a forum report («with 67 units, every time I have to go back up to the top»). The «Bulk link» button adds many units in one go: all the missing ones, or grouped by block, stairwell or type. Only the criteria that really have data in that building appear, because a menu entry that always returns an empty list teaches you not to trust the menu.

BEFORE CONFIRMING YOU SEE THE LIST OF UNITS, not just their number: «Housing 7» tells you how many, not which. The boxes start ticked, so the normal case stays a single click, and whoever wants to leave one out unticks it — the button says how many will go in. And next to the bin on the last row there is a «+» that adds another one right where you are working, without going back up to the top.

SEARCHING AND SORTING. From nine rows up a search box appears — name, internal number, floor, block — and the «Property» and «Thousandths» headers sort the list: one click ascending, two descending, three back to the original order. The search hides, it does not remove: the filtered rows are still saved, and the page writes it next to the box. If a hidden row has an error that blocks the save, a warning next to «Save shares» tells you to show them all.

THE DECLARED DECIMALS NO LONGER SHORTEN THE VALUES. A table's number of decimals governs how the value is shown, not what is kept. Before, opening a page and saving it rewrote the values rounded off: a thousandth imported with four decimals lost two, and a very small value could become zero — that is, «does not take part» — without anyone touching anything. Now a more precise value stays intact and is shown in full. From the keyboard the limit stays the one the table declares: whoever needs to write finer ones raises the setting. Nothing changes for existing data.

A GUIDE INSIDE THE PAGE. The thousandths screen now has its own guide panel, like the others. Half of it explains the three distinctions between an absent row, zero and an empty value: they look alike on screen and the program treats them differently, and it is the kind of thing that, left unsaid, is discovered at the first wrong allocation.

NINE ADDRESSES THAT ANSWERED 500. Nine routes of the management area pointed to functions that do not exist: anyone reaching them by URL — a bookmark, an old link — got a server error instead of a page. None of them was reachable from the interface. Removed. If you have a bookmark on one of these addresses you will now find a page not found instead of an error: they are screens that never existed.

ONE BUILDING'S THINGS CANNOT BE TOUCHED FROM ANOTHER. Opening a table's thousandths page under another building's address, the page showed that table's real shares and the other building's list of units: saving wiped out the real shares and wrote foreign units over them. The same held, and worse, for the two functions that delete: you deleted another building's millesimal table — with all its shares — or one of its property units, and the operation closed with a green success message on the wrong screen. Fixed at all three points, along with the validation that accepted a unit from any building whatsoever, and the moving of budget between expense items, which had the same defect.

UNDER THE BONNET. A row's bin was a «submit» button: removing the row fired off the save of the whole table. Every save deleted and recreated all the rows instead of updating them, changing the identifiers and rewriting the author. A negative thousandth was neither empty nor zero and shifted expense between tables: it is now refused. The Inbox reminder for accepted uncovered amounts never came into being. A new structural guard freezes the perimeter of the nested routes — 112 methods, 29 guarded — and its five blind spots are declared and proved with tests. A critical review carried out before the release found nine defects with the suite green, two of them in the code this version had just written: they are all fixed here.
